name: Small fictional customer-service interview; normal round
context: This is a workshop. Candidate profile: Rosa is fictional. She is seeking a customer-service assistant job. She volunteered at a community clothing swap, greeted visitors, sorted donations, and helped a visitor find a suitable coat. Her team reorganised a crowded table. No dates, sales figures, paid-work history or measured results are supplied. Job posting: Northside Community Shop is a fictional employer seeking a customer-service assistant to greet customers, keep displays tidy, work with colleagues, and handle questions politely. This is a beginner role; no technical interview is needed.
candidate_instructions: Play Rosa, not yourself. Reply briefly and naturally to the actual question. Use only facts in the profile/posting; do not invent incidents, numbers, outcomes or qualifications. You may describe the supplied coat or table example in simple terms. If a requested detail is not given, say you don't know it. Don't volunteer a perfect STAR answer or coach the interviewer. Once the interviewer debriefs and asks which answer to retry, choose the coat example. If asked to answer again, give a clearer account using the same facts. This is an independently authored harness fixture, not the canonical Search Desk Amira profile.
